changes.before: Replace is.na with is.finite. What prints?
changes.after: NA means missing. NaN means not a number, such as the result of an undefined calculation. Inf means infinity.

before: NA represents missing information. NaN represents an undefined numeric result. Inf and -Inf represent positive and negative infinity.
is.na is TRUE for NA and NaN, but FALSE for Inf and ordinary finite values. Comparing a value with NA does not establish whether it is missing.

is.finite(values) takes a numeric vector and returns one logical flag per value: TRUE for finite values and FALSE for NA, NaN and infinities.


```r
values <- c(2, NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf)
cat(is.finite(values), sep = ",")
```
It prints:
```text
TRUE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE,FALSE
```

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:

```r
values <- c(NA, NaN, Inf, 1)
cat(is.na(values), sep=",")
```
